## Dataset-aware model explanations

TrainLens 0.15.0 adds dataset evidence to the same notebook-first workflow used to understand training runs.

### Explain the dataset locally

Use the new deterministic `explain_dataset()` API to summarize the data behind model metrics without deploying a profiler or adding a pandas/Hugging Face dependency:

```python
from trainlens import explain_dataset

dataset_context = explain_dataset(
    {
        "train": train_dataset,
        "validation": validation_dataset,
        "test": test_dataset,
    },
    target="label",
)

dataset_context
```

TrainLens reports aggregate split sizes, feature kinds, missingness, cardinality, numeric ranges and means, average text lengths, target distributions, schema differences, and material target-distribution differences across splits.

The profile is deliberately aggregate-only: raw feature rows are not rendered. Dataset observations are descriptive context and are never presented as proof that a dataset property caused a model result.

### Use dataset evidence when explaining results

A `DatasetExplanation` can now be explicitly supplied to request previews and optional LLM reports:

```python
preview = preview_llm_request(
    globals(),
    mode="improvement_ideas",
    provider=llm,
    dataset_explanation=dataset_context,
)

report = build_improvement_ideas(
    globals(),
    provider=llm,
    dataset_explanation=dataset_context,
)
```

TrainLens does not silently send the underlying dataset. Only the deterministic aggregate explanation is appended, and the combined outbound context remains bounded by `ContextPolicy`.

### Verified dataset evidence

`build_verified_improvement_plan()` can use the same dataset explanation. Split sizes, feature summaries, target summaries, and dataset observations receive stable evidence IDs alongside model metrics and training signals, so invented dataset citations are flagged instead of silently accepted.

### Documentation and Colab

The README now presents dataset explanation as part of the core workflow, a dedicated dataset-aware analysis guide documents privacy and interpretation limits, and the Colab quickstart demonstrates the complete flow from dataset context and training diagnosis to an evidence-backed next-experiment plan.
